2607.14989.title: OmniaBench: Benchmarking General AI Agents Across Diverse Scenarios
2607.14989.paper_summary: Large language models are increasingly evolving from text generators into general agents capable of understanding user requests, invoking external tools, and completing complex tasks through interaction. However, existing agent benchmarks often focus on limited scenarios, tool ecosystems, or interaction formats, making it difficult to systematically characterize model capabilities across heterogeneous application settings. We introduce OmniaBench, a benchmark for evaluating general agents across diverse scenarios with explicit state spaces. We derive application-oriented scenario knowledge from app stores, product documents, industry resources, Web retrieval, and human refinement, forming a hierarchical taxonomy that spans ToC, ToB and ToE with 90 level-1 and 354 level-2 domains. Based on this taxonomy, we construct executable environments and synthesize single-turn and multi-turn tasks through four complementary routes: DAG, DAG-S, Solver, and Program. OmniaBench further introduces a ten-dimensional capability taxonomy and eight compositional atomic difficulty factors to support fine-grained evaluation and analysis. The resulting dataset contains 1,431 tasks, together with a challenging subset of 644 tasks designed to reduce evaluation cost and mitigate potential contamination of the full set after public release. The bench presents substantial challenges to current frontier models, with even Claude-Sonnet-5 and GPT-5.6-Sol achieving Overall Pass@1 scores of only 58.54 and 57.14, respectively. Further analyses reveal clear differences across domains and capabilities, as well as persistent limitations in planning, constraint maintenance, and adaptive correction. OmniaBench provides a broad and diagnostic benchmark for characterizing the capability boundaries of general agents.
2607.14989.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型正逐漸從文本生成器演變為能夠理解用戶請求、調用外部工具並通過互動完成複雜任務的一般代理。<lb/>然而，現有的代理基準通常專注於有限的場景、工具生態系統或互動格式，這使得在異質應用設置中系統性地表徵模型能力變得困難。<lb/>我們介紹了OmniaBench，這是一個用於在多樣化場景中評估一般代理的基準，具有明確的狀態空間。<lb/>我們從應用商店、產品文檔、行業資源、網絡檢索和人類精煉中提取以應用為導向的場景知識，形成了一個層次化的分類法，涵蓋了ToC、ToB和ToE，共有90個一級和354個二級領域。<lb/>基於這一分類法，我們構建了可執行的環境，並通過四條互補路徑合成單輪和多輪任務：DAG、DAG-S、Solver和Program。<lb/>OmniaBench進一步引入了一個十維的能力分類法和八個組合原子難度因素，以支持細緻的評估和分析。<lb/>最終的數據集包含1,431個任務，還有一個挑戰性的子集，其中包含644個任務，旨在降低評估成本並減少在公開發布後對完整數據集的潛在污染。<lb/>該基準對當前前沿模型提出了重大挑戰，即使是Claude-Sonnet-5和GPT-5.6-Sol的整體通過率@1分數也僅為58.54和57.14。<lb/>進一步分析顯示，在不同領域和能力之間存在明顯差異，以及在規劃、約束維護和自適應修正方面的持續限制。<lb/>OmniaBench提供了一個廣泛且診斷性的基準，用於表徵一般代理的能力邊界。
